observations: The source blank slab and attached rectangular plates are replaced by coherent substantial worn stones with broad turning planes and irregular recessed joints. This is a material visible improvement in N/E/S/W at logical128 and phone32 cell pitch.

The crown and broad upper surfaces remain cyan-blue; deeper cobalt lower stones still carry discernible form. The original almost-black bottom band and thin artificial finished-end stripe are gone. Native+X exposed-end detail, visible most directly in W, now reads as an irregular recessed stone course inside the connector plane.

Soft broad highlights and rounded facet transitions fit the selected cartoon direction. There is no visible horizontal lighting preference, directional ground shadow, glossy white stripe, clipped silhouette, floating plate or material black dead spot in the required views.

The middle–edge–middle contexts keep the edge distinctive through a different large stone layout while surface color and form shading continue across both shared interfaces. Both joins remain visually continuous in native and current SpriteScene views; the change of stone pattern does not become an extra border, alpha crack, crown step or lighting reset.

remainingDifferences: The fixed target has more swollen individual stones, stronger painterly edge accents and more small pebbles. The native result uses broader, quieter carved facets and restrained end detail, consistent with the approved shared family material. Those differences do not prevent the required style improvement.

Exact functional end profiles retain a geometric crown-to-side transition and modular cut planes. The native highlights are softer and less white than the target; copying the target outline or directional-looking highlight ribbons would conflict with locked continuity or lighting.

The lower surface remains deliberately darker than the upper rock, but its stone structure remains visible at use size. Mixed native versus independent publication has small retained antialiasing/sample residuals, without a perceptible join defect.
